title: ATM domain model
idea: The ATM domain model separates the machine (ATM, CashDispenser, ATMState) from the bank's records (Card, Account, Transaction), joined only through BankService.

analogy.text: A shop till and the bank behind it. The till holds notes and knows its own mode; the bank holds accounts and the ledger.
analogy.breaks: A till pays out without asking; an ATM needs the bank's approval first.

points: An ATM owns one CashDispenser and has exactly one ATMState at a time.
A Card points to one Account; the ATM holds zero or one Card.
Account owns the balance; only `debit` may lower it, never below zero.
A Transaction records type, amount in paise and status for one Account.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: Each ATM owns one CashDispenser: a map from note value to how many notes are loaded.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: ATMState says what the machine is doing now. Page 4 turns it into a state machine.

edges.label: holds 0..1
edges.caption: At most one Card is inside the machine during a session.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: The ATM never touches an Account directly. It asks BankService over the network.

edges.label: manages *
edges.caption: BankService owns every Account. It is the only code that calls debit.

edges.label: links 1
edges.caption: A Card links to one Account by id. Several cards may share an account.

edges.label: records *
edges.caption: Every debit or reversal the bank performs is written as a Transaction.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: TransactionStatus moves PENDING to COMPLETED or REVERSED. DECLINED records a refusal.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for data that never changes, classes for Account and CashDispenser because their numbers change. Invariants live in constructors and methods.

walk.text: A Card prints a masked number and knows when it expires.
Debit Rs 2,000 from an account holding Rs 5,000.
Load notes in any order; the dispenser keeps them largest first.
Two refusals: overdrawing the account, and a zero-amount withdrawal.
`toString` shows only the last four digits, so logs never leak a card number.
Balance is private. `debit` is the only way down, and it refuses to overdraw.
A reverse-ordered `TreeMap` keeps note order fixed, and negative counts are refused.

pitfalls: Do not give the ATM a direct Account reference; balances live at the bank.
Never print or log a full card number; mask all but the last four digits.
Store money and note values as long paise; double cannot hold exact paise.

quiz.q: What does the third line of AtmModel print?
quiz.why: The TreeMap uses reverse order, so the largest note prints first. The total stays in paise, and a new ATM starts IDLE.

takeaway: The machine holds notes and state; the bank holds accounts and the ledger.

starters: Why is BankService an interface and not a class?
Should Card hold the PIN, or only the bank?
How would I model a joint account with two cards?
